overall: Declined to review the November 19 complaint as untimely, found no Open Meeting Law violation on the December 3 escrow-deliberation complaint, and declined non-Open Meeting Law and non-member allegations.

allegations.summary: Nov. 19 complaint alleged the Commission deliberated outside a noticed meeting on adding LEC to a preapproval list and requesting its proposal for 0 Lakeshore Center.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the November 19 complaint was not timely filed with the Commission and we must decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Dec. 3 complaint alleged the Commission deliberated outside a noticed meeting to decide not to require an escrow account to pay LEC for the 0 Lakeshore Center project.
allegations.key_passage: Absent sufficient evidence to the contrary, we credit a public body’s account of the facts, and we find here that the Commission did not deliberate outside of a noticed meeting as alleged.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that the Community Economic Development Director, who is not a Commission member, violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Mr. Rulli is not a member of the Commission; therefore, to the extent the complaint alleges that Mr. Rulli violated the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaints raised procurement procedure and wetlands bylaw compliance concerns, which are outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review these allegations where, even if true, they would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
